concerns.text: T008 targets only TinyLlama-1.1B for the primary CI path, explicitly excluding 7B models. This silently weakens US-1 and FR-001 which mandate generation across 'two open-source LLM checkpoints'. The task delivers a subset of the required data acquisition scope.

T020 implements Cohen's κ calculation and sensitivity analysis but omits the mandatory step in FR-010 to 'report correlation between human coherence ratings and automated validity scores'. The task satisfies the reliability check but fails the validation correlation requirement.

T012 implements a 'control corpus' of technical reports. Neither FR-001, US-1, nor the spec's acceptance criteria mention generating control data. This introduces unapproved scope (scope creep) that dilutes the research focus on phenomenological reports.

T028 implements 'internal state tracing' (activations/attention maps). The spec and plan define validity metrics solely via NLI, embeddings, and markers. Capturing internal states is not required for the defined metrics and violates the principle of not introducing unverified empirical capabilities.

Tasks T045-T049 implement advanced features (Turing test, latent traces, embodiment gap) based on simulated reviewer comments. These capabilities are absent from the spec's User Stories and Functional Requirements, representing significant retroactive narrowing of the project scope to unapproved philosophical experiments.

T013 handles NLI length limits by 'skipping pairs' but lacks a mechanism to track report-level completion rates. SC-001 requires metrics for ≥95% of reports; without a task to enforce or verify this threshold, the acceptance criterion is silently weakened.
